results.answer: For NordChemica, the 30-day target for actionable alerts is to reduce them to 500 or fewer per day. Additionally, there is a promise of an immediate reduction of 70% in actionable alerts within 7 days of deploying the suppression tuning bundle [art_0a135c689c08, art_ffa7143fb822].

The NordChemica remediation plan proposes an EN-DEDUPE sliding-window setting of 5 minutes (300 seconds) with pattern-based grouping by service, host, and event type. Additionally, the per-host rate limit set for heartbeat-missing-v1 is 1 per minute. These settings are part of the suppression tuning bundle scheduled for delivery on 2026-03-22 to reduce noisy alerting and improve alert signal quality [art_ffa7143fb822].

The contractual financial remedy offered to NordChemica is a conditional 6% credit on their contract for the next year. This credit is tied to specific success metrics: reducing actionable alerts by 70% within 7 days and achieving less than or equal to 500 actionable alerts per day within 30 days after deployment of the suppression tuning bundle. These improvements are measured against an agreed analytics baseline report (SIQ-ALERT-ANALYTICS baseline report) that is to be delivered before the tuning bundle deployment to establish the reference point for measuring alert reduction. If these targets are not met, the 6% credit will be applied as a financial concession [art_ffa7143fb822].

For Aurora University's Ontario campus, the temporary Signal Ingest transform (SI-ETL-FILTER) populates canonical.student_id by concatenating the region_code, a hyphen, and the local.student_number, but only if the event contains local.student_number and does not already have canonical.student_id. This transform preserves the original local.student_number field, making the mapping non-destructive. Additionally, the transform adds a metadata field ingest.transform_version with the value "aurora-v1". This transform is scoped only to the aurora tenant as a short-term fix pending migration to a central identity service within 6 weeks. The schema registry version is bumped and registered with backward compatibility to record this change [art_db3975cc8475].

The rollback window for the Aurora Ontario production deploy is 60 minutes. The automatic safeguard that triggers a disable is if more than 2% message drop is observed during the deploy [art_db3975cc8475].

The mapping events failed primarily because the 'role' attribute was missing in about 30% of the ServiceNow 'store' catalog webhooks, and in other cases, the role was present but under a legacy key 'job_code' for the corporate catalog. This inconsistency in attribute naming caused SCIM mapping failures and fragmented approval chains across departments. Additionally, the ServiceNow webhook variants were not harmonized, leading to approximately 9,000 failed mapping events out of 28,000 provisioning events following the HR restructure effective 2026-02-15 [art_ab3362f35c1b, art_ff2f6b934213, art_fceed52dcb35].

Northstar recommended a fix involving immediate staging of an ETL normalization rule named SI-ETL-FILTER to map the legacy 'job_code' key to the canonical 'role' attribute and to provide fallback heuristics for missing roles. This rule would tag all normalized events and was planned to be staged in a non-production environment starting 2026-03-19, tested, and then deployed to production upon approval. Alongside this, Northstar proposed implementing an Orchestrator playbook to automatically retry failed provisioning events for the store catalog and perform dry-run re-triggers for corporate catalog events. The playbook would include safe rollback capabilities and audit logging (OR-SAFE-ROLLBACK and OR-AUDIT-LOGS) to ensure safe remediation and traceability. A Signal Insights dashboard was also to be built to monitor provisioning latency, failed mapping counters, and collector health, with the first snapshot scheduled for 2026-03-26. Finally, a retention policy change to extend provisioning log retention to 365 days was recommended to support auditability, pending commercial amendment approval [art_ab3362f35c1b, art_ff2f6b934213, art_3fb93065ab3e].

This remediation plan aimed to reduce the median provisioning latency from about 18 hours back toward pre-change levels of approximately 3.5 hours and to provide audit evidence for board reporting by 2026-04-15 [art_ab3362f35c1b].

results.answer:
If the validation checks fail for Verdant Bay's live patch, the system automatically executes a rollback to the prior ruleset. The rollback procedure uses the command `orchestrator rollback --target ruleset=<prior_sha>`, which rehydrates the prior rules and replays the cache invalidation hook to restore the previous state. After rollback, the team notifies Verdant Bay, opens an incident for manual remediation, and reverts any partial replays that may have occurred. This rollback plan is integrated into the live patch steps scheduled for 2026-03-24 from 02:00 to 04:00 local time, which includes a pre-patch snapshot and draining of the worker pool to ensure safe deployment and rollback capability. The validation jobs that trigger rollback include running 50 synthetic approval flows and a sample of 50 in-flight approvals marked by the customer; if any of these validations fail, rollback is triggered automatically [art_fff67d92fe41]. 

No detailed step-by-step commands beyond the `orchestrator rollback` command are provided, nor are there specifics on timing or monitoring during rollback beyond the general procedure. The rollback trigger is any failure in the validation checks without further detailed criteria or thresholds given [art_fff67d92fe41].
